profileHelp.title: The four profiles
profileHelp.desc: Wizard step 3 offers Minimal, Pruned, Validator-ready, and RPC. They differ by disk and role. The wizard shows the size for the chain you picked. The panel never holds staking keys.
profileHelp.useMinimal: Testnet or a first install. Not a full history.
profileHelp.usePruned: Follow the chain tip long-term. Keeps recent data only (Pruned).
profileHelp.useValidatorReady: Sized so you can later attest or propose. Generate keys offline yourself.
profileHelp.useRpc: Let this host or other services query the chain. Listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.
profileHelp.stakeYes: Yes — offline or misconfigured can lose stake
profileHelp.minimal: Smallest disk. Use for testnets or a first install. Not a full history, and not for a live staking validator.
profileHelp.pruned: Keeps recent chain state and drops older blocks (Pruned). More disk than Minimal, less than a full node. Use to follow the tip long-term.
profileHelp.validatorReady: Reserves more disk so you can later attest or propose as a validator. Generate keys offline yourself. Being offline or misconfigured can lose stake.
profileHelp.rpc: For this host or other services to query the chain. RPC listens on 127.0.0.1 by default and is not published to the internet.

playbook.overviewTitle: How staking works on each chain
playbook.overviewDesc: This panel runs the node. Your wallet and keys stay with you. Official links only — never share a seed phrase here.
playbook.seeAbout: Full steps are on the About tab.
playbook.nodeIdPending: NodeID appears after the node is synced and answering RPC.
playbook.blsPending: BLS credentials appear after the node answers RPC.
playbook.nearStakeKeyPending: Appears after first start (neard init). RPC not ready does not mean the key is missing.
playbook.nearAccountIdPending: Often empty until you set it to {pool}{{suffix}} yourself. This panel never writes validator_key.json.
playbook.nearPublicAddrPending: Appears after first start writes WAN:{{port}} into config.json.
playbook.nearPointing: The pool contract does not take this server’s IP. It stores this node’s stake public key. Peers use the Public P2P row above (host port {{port}}). RPC stays on localhost.
playbook.nearAccountIdHint: After the pool exists, set account_id in validator_key.json to {pool}{{suffix}} yourself. This panel never writes that file.
playbook.cosmosPubkeyPending: Appears after gaiad init writes priv_validator_key.json. RPC not ready does not mean the key is missing.
playbook.cosmosP2pPending: Appears after first start writes tcp://WAN:{{port}} into config.toml.
playbook.ethBeaconPending: Beacon HTTP on this host. Point a validator client you run yourself at this URL — this compose has no VC.
playbook.solIdentityPending: Appears after RPC answers getIdentity. This process is --no-voting until you add a vote account yourself.
playbook.adaP2pPending: Put this host’s public IPv4 and this port in topology.json. This panel does not probe WAN.
playbook.notPosBody: Bitcoin here is a full or pruned node. There is no staking wallet on this page.

eth.model: This compose runs execution + beacon only — not a validator client. Deposit 32 ETH on the official launchpad.
eth.wallets: MetaMask, Ledger, Trezor — only on the official launchpad
eth.panel: Runs EL + beacon. RPC and beacon API on localhost. No validator client in compose.
eth.honesty: This instance is execution + beacon only. There is no validator client in the compose file. Copying a keystore into the beacon data directory will not start attesting. The deposit contract does not take this server’s IP.
yskDoes: Install and start the execution and beacon clients.
Show disk, peers, and upgrade status.
Does not run a validator client and does not load a signing keystore.
youDo: Create the keystore and withdrawal address yourself on the official launchpad or with staking-deposit-cli.
Deposit 32 ETH on the launchpad for this network.
Run a validator client yourself (not this compose) against this instance’s localhost beacon API.
steps: Wait until execution and beacon are synced.
Open the official launchpad for this network (Hoodi or Mainnet on this page). Sepolia has no launchpad button here.
Offline, generate the keystore. Set the withdrawal address to your own ETH wallet.
Deposit 32 ETH (keep extra for gas).
Run a validator client yourself. This compose has no VC — putting a keystore in the beacon datadir does not attest.
never: Never give your seed phrase or withdrawal key to anyone, including this panel.
Never upload a signing keystore to a hosted cloud.
Do not expect this page to attest after you copy a keystore into the beacon datadir.

avax.model: Register the running NodeID and BLS proof on the P-Chain from Core or Ledger.
avax.min: 2,000 AVAX + fee (1 AVAX on Fuji); at least 14 days
avax.panel: Runs avalanchego and can show NodeID and BLS after RPC answers
yskDoes: Run avalanchego and keep RPC on localhost.
Show NodeID and BLS credentials once the node answers RPC.
youDo: Hold AVAX in Core or Ledger.
Add the validator from Core using this node’s NodeID and BLS proof.
steps: Wait until this node is synced.
Copy the NodeID, BLS public key, and BLS proof of possession shown on the instance page.
In Core web (Staking → Validate), or with Ledger via Core, register on the P-Chain.
Mainnet needs at least 2,000 AVAX, a 14-day minimum period, and a fee reserve.
never: Do not send AVAX to this panel.
Do not share your Core or Ledger recovery phrase.

ada.model: Operate a stake pool with offline cold / KES / VRF keys — not a browser wallet tap.
ada.min: Pledge is your choice (see official docs)
ada.wallets: Official stake-pool tooling (cold keys stay offline)
ada.panel: Runs cardano-node as a relay first; hot keys can be attached on this page.
ada.honesty: This instance starts as a relay. On-chain pool registration uses cold keys you keep offline. Peers and topology use this host’s public IPv4 and the P2P port shown here — the panel does not probe WAN.
yskDoes: Run cardano-node and Mithril snapshot restore where offered.
Attach KES, VRF, and opcert when you provide them. Cold keys are refused.
youDo: Generate pool keys offline.
Register the pool using official Cardano documentation.
Put this host’s public IPv4 and the relay P2P port into topology.json.
steps: Read the official operate-a-stake-pool guide.
Generate cold, KES, and VRF keys on an offline machine.
Register the pool on-chain from those keys.
On this instance page, attach KES, VRF, and the operational certificate. Do not upload cold keys.
Advertise the relay as public-ip:P2P-port (port shown on this card). This panel does not look up the WAN address.
never: Do not treat this as a MetaMask one-click stake.
Do not store cold keys on the validator host.

near.model: Create a staking-pool contract at the official factory. The contract stores this node’s public key — not the server IP.
near.min: See official validator docs (30 NEAR to create the pool, plus stake)
near.panel: Runs neard; shows the public key, factory, and create_staking_pool command after init
yskDoes: Run neard with RPC on localhost and P2P on 24567.
After init, show the stake public key, public P2P address, factory, and a copyable create_staking_pool command.
Never write validator_key.json or broadcast the transaction.
youDo: Copy the public key and command from this instance page.
From your own NEAR account, call the official factory.
After the pool exists, set account_id in validator_key.json to {pool}.{factory} yourself.
Stake from your wallet into that pool.
steps: Start the node and wait for neard init so the public key appears (RPC not ready is not the same as missing keys).
Copy the stake public key and the create_staking_pool command.

From your wallet, call the factory (testnet pool.f863973.m0 / mainnet poolv1.near) with 30 NEAR for storage. The copied command uses --accountId; if your near CLI expects --account_id, follow that CLI’s --help.
Set account_id in validator_key.json to your new pool account. This panel does not write that file.
Wait until RPC answers and the node is synced before staking large amounts. Peers use Public P2P :24567 — the contract does not take an IP.
never: Do not paste a seed phrase into this panel.
Do not put this server’s IP into the contract.
Do not expect the panel to send the create_staking_pool transaction.

cosmos.model: create-validator from your operator wallet using this node’s consensus public key — not the server IP.
cosmos.min: See official Cosmos Hub docs (self-delegation in uatom)
cosmos.wallets: Keplr or another Cosmos wallet you control
cosmos.panel: Runs gaiad; shows consensus pubkey and a copyable create-validator command after init
cosmos.honesty: The create-validator transaction stores this node’s consensus public key. Peers use Public P2P on 26656. RPC stays on localhost. This panel does not broadcast the transaction or read priv_key.
yskDoes: Run gaiad with RPC on localhost and P2P on 26656.
After init, show the consensus public key, chain-id, public P2P, and a copyable create-validator command.
Never write priv_validator_key.json or broadcast the transaction.
youDo: Copy the consensus public key and command from this instance page.
From your operator wallet (Keplr or gaiad keys you control), submit create-validator.
Do not mix that wallet mnemonic with the consensus key on this host.
steps: Start the node and wait for gaiad init so the consensus public key appears (RPC not ready is not the same as missing keys).
Copy the consensus public key and the create-validator command (chain-id is cosmoshub-4 on mainnet, provider on testnet).
From your operator wallet, broadcast create-validator. Amount and moniker are yours.
Wait until RPC answers and the node is synced before bonding large amounts. Peers use tcp://WAN:26656 — the transaction does not take an IP.
never: Do not mix the operator wallet mnemonic with the consensus key.
Do not enter wallet mnemonics here.
Do not put this server’s IP into create-validator.

sol.model: This compose runs Agave with --no-voting. Vote account and withdrawer are created with official Solana tools — not this panel.
sol.min: See official operations docs (hardware and disk are heavy)
sol.wallets: Official Solana CLI / wallet you control
sol.panel: Runs Agave as a catch-up node (--no-voting). Can show identity pubkey after RPC answers.
sol.honesty: This process is --no-voting. It will not vote or earn stake until you create a vote account with official Agave CLI and change how the process is started. This panel does not remove --no-voting.
yskDoes: Run the Agave client and warn about disk.
Show the identity pubkey once RPC answers getIdentity.
Does not create a vote account and does not start voting.
youDo: Create vote and authorized-withdrawer keys with official Solana tools on a machine you control.
Create the vote account with the official CLI, using this identity pubkey.
Only then run a voting validator — this compose stays --no-voting.
steps: Confirm this host has enough disk and IOPS (mainnet is typically 2 TiB+).
Wait until RPC answers, then copy the identity pubkey shown here.
Follow official vote-account and stake guides (links below).
This compose keeps --no-voting. Do not expect this page to start voting after you create a vote account.
never: Do not expect a browser wallet button in this panel.
Do not paste identity or vote keypairs into this panel.

dot.model: This compose is a full node (no --validator). Session keys and setKeys are official Polkadot.js steps — not this panel.
dot.panel: Runs polkadot as a full node. RPC on localhost. No --validator flag.
dot.honesty: This process is not started with --validator. The panel does not call author_rotateKeys (that would change the keystore). Becoming a validator needs the official node flag and a rotateKeys call you make against localhost RPC.
yskDoes: Run polkadot and expose RPC on localhost.
Does not pass --validator and does not rotate session keys.
youDo: Follow the official set-up-a-validator guide.
If you add --validator yourself, call rotateKeys on localhost RPC and bind the result in Polkadot.js from your stash.
steps: Sync this full node.
Read the official validate guide. This compose is not a validator process.
Do not paste the stash mnemonic here. If you later run with --validator, rotate keys yourself on http://127.0.0.1 (RPC port on this instance).
In Polkadot.js, set those session keys on your stash / controller, then follow official bonding steps.
never: Do not paste the stash mnemonic into this panel.
Do not expect this page to generate session keys or to have started --validator.

sui.model: This compose is a Sui fullnode (fullnode.yaml), not a validator node.
sui.panel: Runs sui-node as a fullnode. RPC on localhost.
sui.honesty: This process cannot sign as a Sui validator. Validator setup uses a different config and keys. Official validator docs are linked; this panel does not switch the node to validator mode.
yskDoes: Run the shipped sui-node image as a fullnode.
youDo: Use this instance as a fullnode.
To become a validator, follow official Sui validator docs on a validator config — not this compose.
steps: Sync this fullnode.
Treat it as a fullnode: it re-executes checkpoints but does not sign consensus.
Open the official validator operator guide only if you are building a separate validator process.
never: Do not send SUI to this panel.
Do not expect this fullnode process to register as a validator.

aptos.model: This compose is an Aptos public fullnode (role full_node), not a validator.
aptos.panel: Runs aptos-node as a public fullnode. RPC on localhost.
aptos.honesty: Public fullnodes do not participate in consensus. A validator needs a different role, keys, and usually a validator fullnode. This panel does not switch the node to validator mode.
yskDoes: Run the shipped Aptos image as a public fullnode.
youDo: Use this instance as a public fullnode.
To run a validator, follow official Aptos validator-node docs — not this compose.
steps: Sync this public fullnode.
Treat it as a PFN: it serves ledger data, it does not vote.
Open official validator docs only if you are building a separate validator + VFN pair.
never: Do not enter operator keys in this panel.
Do not expect this fullnode process to register as a validator.

btc.model: Not proof-of-stake. This is a Bitcoin full or pruned node.
yskDoes: Run a Bitcoin full or pruned node.
youDo: Use any Bitcoin wallet separately. Mining and Lightning are out of scope.
steps: Treat this instance as a Bitcoin node only.
There is no staking deposit and no validator keystore.
never: Do not look for a staking wallet on this page.
